cfo.title: Florida DOGE audits launched: Broward County and City of Gainesville
cfo.summary: DeSantis and Ingoglia announce first on-site DOGE reviews of local spending, targeting Broward County and Gainesville.

cfo.title: CFO demands local governments comply with DOGE review
cfo.summary: Ingoglia warns cities and counties to comply with DOGE document requests without red tape; later alleges data scrubbing ahead of audits.

cfo.title: Florida DOGE records request to Miami-Dade County
cfo.summary: DOGE requests contracts, salaries, climate projects, grants and DEI records to probe a $402M county deficit; Aug 13 deadline with possible financial penalties. No findings at this stage.

cfo.title: Subpoenas issued to Orange County employees over DOGE audit obstruction
cfo.summary: DeSantis and Ingoglia announce subpoenas of Orange County employees accused of obstructing the state DOGE audit.

cfo.title: FAFO: Orange County flagged ~$200M 'wasteful' spending
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims nearly $200M excess spending; calls for millage cut. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: City of Jacksonville flagged $200M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims $200M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Hillsborough County flagged $278M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims over $278M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Alachua County flagged $84M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims over $84M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Broward County flagged $189M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims over $189M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Seminole County flagged $48M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims over $48M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Manatee County flagged $112M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims over $112M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: City of Miami flagged $94M 'excessive, wasteful' spending
cfo.summary: Claims $94M excess in City of Miami General Fund (up $358M / 44% since FY19-20); urges 0.50-mill cut. No penalty or referral; no vendors named. AFP and LIBRE spoke in support.

cfo.title: FAFO: Miami-Dade County flagged $302M (largest of nine reviewed)
cfo.summary: Claims $302M excess in county General Fund (up $843M / 50% since FY19-20; 2,800+ hires in five years); urges 0.53-mill cut. No penalty or referral; no vendors named.

cfo.title: FAFO: City of Orlando flagged $22M
cfo.summary: FAFO budget review claims $22M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: FAFO: Palm Beach County flagged $344M
cfo.summary: FAFO claims $344M excess; county administrator disputed the figures. No penalty.

cfo.title: Miami Beach operational audit ordered (Auditor General via JLAC, not CFO/DOGE)
cfo.summary: JLAC approved Basabe's request for an Auditor General operational audit of Miami Beach (procurement, sister-cities travel). Reporting says it is unrelated to Ingoglia's DOGE. Included only because Miami Beach was asked about.

cfo.title: Proposal to codify the Florida Agency for Fiscal Oversight (FAFO)
cfo.summary: Ingoglia proposes putting FAFO in statute; Dec 18 adds local budget standardization proposals.

cfo.title: FAFO: City of St. Petersburg flagged $49M
cfo.summary: FAFO claims over $49M excess spending. No penalty.

cfo.title: CFO's local government budget bill (HB 1329) clears Legislature
cfo.summary: Bill increases transparency/standardization in local government budgeting.

cfo.title: FAFO: Miami-Dade County FY25-26 budget flagged $470M
cfo.summary: Claims $470M excess in FY25-26 budget and $807M over three years; urges 0.83-mill cut tied to November property-tax ballot measure. No penalty or referral; no vendors named.

cfo.title: FAFO: Palm Beach County FY25-26 flagged $443M
cfo.summary: FAFO claims over $443M excess. No penalty. (Also 2026 reports on Nassau $53M, Fort Pierce $10M, Citrus $39M, Flagler $59M, St. Lucie $46M, Orange $300M, Jacksonville $275M, Osceola $165M.)

cfo.title: CFO and AG announce criminal charges against Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa
cfo.summary: DFS and Attorney General announce charges and arrest of Kissimmee's mayor.

cfo.title: OIR fines eight insurers $2.075M over Ian/Idalia claims handling; Ingoglia touts as accountability
cfo.summary: Fines: American Coastal $400K, American Mobile $400K, Centauri $100K, Clear Blue $400K, Monarch $325K, Sutton $50K, Tower Hill Prime $250K, TypTap $150K. Violations: unappointed adjusters, slow claims communication, unpaid interest. Ingoglia announced it at his Sept 2 campaign launch.

cfo.title: OIR fines Slide and Kin $250K each over Ian/Idalia claims
cfo.summary: Slide used unappointed adjusters and skipped disclosures; Kin skipped disclosures and missed 90-day claim deadline. Brings Ian/Idalia exam penalties to $2.575M across 10 companies.

cfo.title: DFS amplifies homeowners rate relief: Citizens -8.7%, Florida Peninsula -8.2%, Security First -8%, Universal -5.1%
cfo.summary: CFO press office re-issues governor's announcement: Citizens average cut 8.7% (Miami-Dade 14%), private carrier cuts, auto cuts.

cfo.title: DFS amplifies auto rate decreases for top five auto groups
cfo.summary: Indicated average -8% for 2026; Progressive ~$1B credits, State Farm -10% and $533M dividend.

cfo.title: OIR immediately suspends Mirra Health
cfo.summary: Suspension for sending sensitive claims/enrollment data to unlicensed entities in India and the Philippines (OIR action, FSC-supervised).

cfo.title: OIR approves homeowners rate decreases
parties: One Alliance North America Insurance Company
cfo.summary: One Alliance -10.4%, Safe Harbor -4.1%, Unique -3.2%, Vyrd -10.4%.

cfo.title: Cease and desist against Hydrogen Deep, LLC (Wave Insurance) for unlicensed activity
cfo.summary: OIR order re-issued by CFO press office.

cfo.title: Ingoglia calls for transparency on insurer payments to affiliates
cfo.summary: At USF press conference, backs disclosure of money flowing between insurers and affiliates (MGAs etc.); cites 2026 HB 1399 (passed House 106-3) and SB 234 (20% cap, no hearing). No insurers named.

cfo.title: OIR forces American Mobile Insurance Exchange to surrender certificate of authority
cfo.summary: Mobile-home insurer in unsound condition (surplus $15.09M) after cancelling 1,100+ policies and trying to redomesticate; surrender ordered after administrative supervision. No new DFS receiverships found for 2025-26.

cfo.title: DFS arrests public adjuster for $703K theft of Hurricane Ian claim funds
cfo.summary: DFS Criminal Investigations: 13 homeowners' settlement checks allegedly diverted; organized fraud and elder exploitation charges; Broward SAO prosecuting. Firm reportedly unlicensed.

cfo.title: Stablecoin Pilot Program (SB 1568 / HB 1415) passes Legislature
cfo.summary: CFO priority: DFS to accept payment stablecoins for licensing and regulatory fees. No companies named.

cfo.title: $24M+ awarded to law enforcement agencies for immigration enforcement
cfo.summary: State Board of Immigration Enforcement reimbursements announced by CFO; recipients are agencies, not vendors.

cfo.title: MOU between Florida Treasury and U.S. DOJ National Fraud Enforcement Division
cfo.summary: Fraud data-sharing MOU. No $1M+ vendor contracts were found in CFO announcements Jul 2025-Oct 2026.

cfo.title: Unclaimed property rebranded 'Claim Your Cash Florida'
cfo.summary: New name and site ClaimYourCashFL.gov; no vendor or contract named.

cfo.title: Financial Services Commission adopts OFR de-banking attestation rules
cfo.summary: Rules 69U-100.323 and 69U-100.3231: annual attestations and enforcement of the statute barring 'unlawful discriminatory practices' (de-banking) by financial institutions. No petitioner named.

cfo.title: Financial Services Commission adopts gold and silver coin rules
cfo.summary: New 69U-100.97 and 69V-560.7032-.7036 implement Ch. 2025-100 (gold/silver coin as legal tender: custody, disclosures, accredited refiners). Subject to legislative ratification.

fdacs.title: FDACS EV charging station readiness standards adopted
fdacs.summary: Final rules omitted pre-wiring requirements for all developers without explanation.

fdacs.title: Cabinet approves Rural and Family Lands easements: Ryals Citrus and Cattle, Williams Property, Headwaters Ranch
fdacs.summary: Ryals Citrus and Cattle (Charlotte, 3,722 ac, $13.2M, half USDA NRCS); Williams Property (Levy, 1,782 ac, $6.06M); Headwaters Ranch (Lake, 993 ac, $6M, 53% SWFWMD).

fdacs.title: 2025 Florida Farm Bill (SB 700) signed
fdacs.summary: Simpson priority: fluoride ban in water, retail fuel registration and generator-switch grants for gas stations, theft/skimmer protections, bars banks from ESG discrimination against farmers, plant-based labeling limits, farmworker housing.

fdacs.title: Amended hemp rule 5K-4.034 enforcement begins
fdacs.summary: Color-additive bans, child-resistant packaging, expanded COAs, marketing limits, flower water-activity standard.

fdacs.title: Operation Safe Summer week 1: ~11,000 hemp packages removed
fdacs.summary: Inspections in 20 counties; no businesses named.

fdacs.title: Operation Safe Summer five-week total: 155,932 packages
fdacs.summary: Running total later reported as 197,303 packages across 67 counties; 1.3M+ since July 2023.

fdacs.title: 2025 RFLPP project cycle: 402 properties under review and ranking
fdacs.summary: Properties shown on FDACS StoryMap; program page linked.

fdacs.title: FDACS drafts rule defining 'cartoon' for hemp products attractive to children
fdacs.summary: Workshop Aug 13, 2025.

fdacs.title: FDACS removes 17,311 packages of 7-OH after AG emergency ban
parties: gas stations, vape shops, convenience stores (unnamed)
fdacs.summary: Removals in 23 counties; no retailers named.

fdacs.title: Emergency rule requires 7-OH concentration labeling on kratom
fdacs.summary: Products over 400 ppm 7-OH pulled from sale; 90-day emergency rule.

fdacs.title: 2025 RFLPP priority list presented to Senate Agriculture: 428 projects, 530,000+ acres, $1.75B
fdacs.summary: $250M current-year appropriation. Full ranked list not in document; named examples only.

fdacs.title: Kip Whaley Ranch protected (~2,300 acres, Madison County)
fdacs.summary: Price not stated in accessible text.

fdacs.title: Cabinet approves Siboney Ranch ($9.85M) and Tilton Family Farm ($5.56M) easements
fdacs.summary: Siboney Ranch, Okeechobee, ~1,059 ac, $9,850,000; Tilton Family Farm, Putnam, ~2,060 ac, $5,564,000. Siboney Ranch gave Simpson's committee $100K in June 2026 (Florida Trib).

fdacs.title: Cabinet approves Square One Ranch and Buckhorn Ranch easements
fdacs.summary: Square One Ranch, Highlands, ~1,500 ac, $6.1M ($2M Air Force REPI); Buckhorn Ranch, Hardee, 1,326 ac, $5.3M.

fdacs.title: 2026 Farm Bill (HB 433 / SB 290): 'food libel' provision dropped
fdacs.summary: Provision letting food producers sue critics, reportedly linked to the sugar industry and field burning, was removed. Bill adds conservation-land surplus review for ag sale.

fdacs.title: Block Grant Disaster Relief Program ($600M+) opens, incl. citrus-only grants
fdacs.summary: FDACS secured USDA funding; up to $200.49/acre; applications Feb 25-Aug 25, 2026.

fdacs.title: FY25-26 citrus funding: $104.5M to CRAFT Foundation (via CRDF), $10M packing equipment cost share
fdacs.summary: Also $6.5M Citrus Health Response Program, $2M budwood (FDACS); $250M RFLPP appropriation.

fdacs.title: Cabinet approves Dixie Ranch West, Thundercloud Ranch, Syfrett Farm & Ranch, LFW Farms easements
fdacs.summary: Dixie Ranch West (Okeechobee, 2,996 ac, $14.2M incl. $2.3M Air Force); Thundercloud (Manatee, 1,042 ac, $11.7M); Syfrett (Highlands, 1,183 ac, $5.3M); LFW Farms (Okeechobee, 1,014 ac, $6.6M).

fdacs.title: No statewide fireworks ban despite drought; Simpson urges responsible use
parties: fireworks retailers (e.g., American Promotional Events/TNT, a donor)
fdacs.summary: Florida Forest Service declined statewide ban.

fdacs.title: FY26-27 citrus funding: $160M CRAFT Foundation, $20M nursery/packing grants, $4.5M CRDF
fdacs.summary: Plus $2M FDACS budwood program.

fdacs.title: Retail Fuel Transfer Switch Modernization Grant Program
fdacs.summary: Up to $10K per station (fiscally constrained counties) / $5K elsewhere; rolling; no awardees published. Created by SB 700.

fdacs.title: Rural and Family Lands Protection Program page (acquisition/priority lists)
fdacs.summary: fdacs.gov blocks automated fetch (robots); priority list must be pulled manually.
